title: Influence of weather events on hypertensive disorders in pregnancy and associated complications. Prospective, controlled, non-interventional study with collection of biomaterials
summary:
Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) are characterised by high blood pressure and can also affect other organ systems, such as the kidneys. These disorders can have a short- and long-term impact on the health of both mother and child. The baby has an increased risk of intrauterine growth retardation, premature birth or, in rare cases, the loss of the child before or after birth. In the long term, children of affected mothers are more susceptible to obesity, diabetes mellitus and cardiovascular diseases. The risk of cardiovascular diseases as well as mental illnesses, especially depression, also increases for the mothers after birth.
Extreme weather events, such as heat waves and increased air pollution, pose a particular threat to vulnerable groups, including pregnant women. Scientific data suggest that there is a link between heat and air pollution and the development of HES. In particular, the timing of heat exposure during pregnancy appears to play a crucial role in the development of the disease. 
The FORESEEN study will investigate the relationships between extreme weather conditions (heat, cold, air pollution) and the development of HDP depending on the week of pregnancy. In addition, the study will investigate whether complications such as preeclampsia, HELLP syndrome, peripartum cardiomyopathy or thrombotic microangiopathy occur and what health consequences they have for mother and child. Another goal is to gain a better understanding of the underlying pathophysiological processes by analysing biomaterials (e.g. maternal blood, cord blood and placental tissue).
To this end, patients who have developed HES and healthy pregnant women with the same characteristics (including age, weight, gestational age) are examined in order to compare these two groups.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Signed written informed consent

Clinically confirmed diagnosis of HDP/associated complications
Pregnant patients with a HDP/associated complication with a singleton pregnancy
Healthy pregnant women with a singleton pregnancy > 37th week of pregnancy
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnant women < 18 years of age
Non-pregnant female patient
Smoking during pregnancy
Multiple pregnancy
Gestational diabetes
Preexisting hypertension
Preexisting nephrological/cardiological/endocrinological disease
Premature rupture of membranes < 37th week of gestation (PPROM)
